claims.summary: The dialogue runtime uses longest exact known-marker matches and preserves marker bytes only when a finite reference syntax is proven.
claims.disposition: Verified from the complete 1,038-line pre-change source. The scanner advances by exact marker byte length or one UTF-8 scalar, reconstructs all non-marker scalars in order, and preserves exact marker bytes only for declared paired delimiters or a finite following relation.

claims.summary: An unsupported nearest non-whitespace punctuation pair can strip a marker that was intended as an explicit reference.
claims.disposition: Verified as a real finite-table boundary. Before this response, vertical CJK presentation-form quotes and several common CJK or fullwidth group pairs returned no reference syntax and therefore removed the exact marker from the remainder.

claims.summary: A marker enclosed by ordinary double quotes should remain visible and classify as a quoted exact-token reference.
claims.disposition: Verified by the existing ASCII quoted-reference regression, which preserves the full input byte-for-byte and records one quoted occurrence, zero removed occurrences, and delimiter depth one.

claims.summary: A marker followed by manifests should remain visible through the explicit-relation path.
claims.disposition: Verified from the finite relation list and the existing poetic-attribution regression, whose relation loop includes manifests and records one following exact relation with no removed marker.

claims.summary: Common Unicode punctuation used across languages should receive exact preservation coverage without broad semantic inference.
claims.disposition: Implemented now by adding two exact vertical CJK quote pairs and six exact CJK or fullwidth grouping pairs. Two regressions prove every pair's classification and a three-level non-whitespace stack while leaving unsupported punctuation fail-closed.
